newsitem.title: USA: GM to consolidate truck operations at Flint, Mich..
newsitem.headline: GM to consolidate truck operations at Flint, Mich..

text.p: General Motors Corp. said Friday it plans to consolidate all of its commercial truck production in Flint, Mich., and discontinue some of its engine and transmission operations there and in Lansing, Mich., affecting about 2,100 employees.

The automaker said it will invest about $500 million in its Flint truck assembly plant for production of GM's commercial and pickup trucks. The number of new jobs to be added was not immediately available.
As part of the investment, GM said it will shift all commercial and medium-duty truck production to Flint from two other plants, in Detroit and Janesville, Wis.

It said it will close the 78-year-old Detroit P-Chassis plant, which builds truck chassis for recreational vehicles, school buses and speciality vans, during the year 2000. Production of those products will be moved to Flint.
GM also said it will move production of medium-duty commercial trucks to Flint from Janesville in 2001.
However, Janesville will continue to be GM's lead plant for full-size sport/utility vehicles, and will build the next generation versions of GM's Tahoe, Yukon and Suburban models.
The moves are designed to increase GM's overall capacity for both medium-duty commercial and light duty trucks.
At the same time, GM said its Powertrain Group will discontinue engineering operations in Lansing and Flint, Mich., by the end of 1998.

Engine and transmission-related engineering activities at the Flint and Lansing locations will be moved to the GM Powertrain Group headquarters in Pontiac and to other locations at GM's proving grounds in Milford, Mich., and its technical centre in Warren, Mich.
In addition, GM said it is relocating administrative employees at the Powertrain Group headquaters into the adjacent former Pontiac Division headquarters.
Pontiac Division employees this year are moving into offices at GM's new global headquarters at the Renaissance Centre in downtown Detroit.
GM's stock slipped 75 cents to $59.625 in midday trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
